subject: ReadySet Health — Finalization & Onboarding Playlist for Private Deploy
messages:
From: Sara Mitchell <sara@readysethealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+readyset@readysethealth.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0000
Subject: ReadySet private deploy — final prerequisites and handoff

Hi Vivek / Ben,

Thanks for the kickoff last week. We are on the home stretch and need to lock down the final prerequisites for our VPC/on‑prem private deployment. Our GA target is Nov 30th and engineering wants a clear list of what you need from us today to avoid last‑minute blockers.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm exact egress IPs and any firewall rules we must add
- Final CIDR ranges you expect for the tenant overlay and control plane
- KMS integration pattern (bring your own key vs. managed) and cert rotation expectations
- Service account roles and example IAM policies for the runtime nodes
- A short acceptance smoke test plan we can run post‑handoff

I attached our current environment inventory and a draft network diagram. Can you reply with a concise checklist and any remaining dependencies we need to resolve? If helpful, we can do a 30m cutover coordination call on Friday.

Sara Mitchell
VP, Infrastructure & Security
ReadySet Health
Attachments: env_inventory.csv (csv), network-diagram.png (image)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mitchell <sara@readysethealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: ReadySet private deploy — final prerequisites and handoff

Sara — thanks for the clear asks. High level: we can meet your timeline but need a handful of items resolved by EOD Wednesday to keep Nov 30th intact. Below is a focused onboarding playlist (concise checklist) and the owner for each item.

Redwood finalization checklist (what we need from ReadySet):
1) Network + IPs (owner: ReadySet netops) — Provide production CIDR for tenant overlay, and confirm any existing customer NAT/egress IPs to allow. We will provide the list of Redwood egress IPs for firewall rules. (Due: Wed 2026-11-18)
2) KMS approach (owner: ReadySet security) — Confirm BYOK or Redwood‑managed KMS and provide key ARN or KMS admin contact. If BYOK, we need a test key and rotation policy.
3) Service accounts & roles (owner: ReadySet cloud team) — One infra service account for provisioning + one runtime service account per cluster. Share minimal IAM policy examples.
4) TLS certs & DNS (owner: ReadySet platform) — Who will own cert issuance and wildcard names for private slices? Provide DNS delegation or route53 zone access if you want us to automate certs.
5) Observability endpoints (owner: ReadySet SRE) — IP/endpoint allowlist for telemetry and where to POST metrics/logs.
6) Acceptance smoke plan (owner: joint) — See proposed smoke checklist below; confirm or edit.

Proposed short smoke acceptance (we need this validated by your SRE before handoff):
- Control plane greeter: auth + basic /health returns 200 within 200ms
- Sample inference: run 100 small requests at p50 latency < 150ms (adjusted for your target)
- KV cache validation: key persistence across restarts
- End‑to‑end logs flow to your logging endpoint (single sample trace)
- Metrics ingestion verified (one metric with expected label set)

Ben and Kim — I’m looping you for the detailed network / KMS steps. I attached a slightly condensed mutual action plan so ReadySet can tick items off. Vivek

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.docx (docx)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mitchell <sara@readysethealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0000
Subject: Re: ReadySet private deploy — final prerequisites and handoff

Sara — adding the concrete network expectations from Redwood side and a minimal ops runbook snippet.

Redwood network deliverables (we will provide):
- Egress IPs: 3 static NAT addresses per region for control plane traffic (will share exact IPs by Wed EOD).
- BGP/Peering: If you prefer direct peering, we can support an IPsec/VPN or Cloud‑to‑Onprem BGP; share your termination details and preference.
- Recommended firewall rules (egress & ingress):
  * Allow outbound 443 to our control plane.. 52.142.XX.XX/32, 34.76.XX.XX/32
  * Allow ingress from Redwood monitoring collectors 10.20.30.0/24 on port 443
- MTU and path MTU guidance: 1500 default; if you run private circuits let us know if you use jumbo frames.

Short ops runbook (activation day):
- Step 1: Validate CIDRs and route tables — confirm no overlap with customer internal ranges
- Step 2: Apply firewall allowlist and NAT rules (ReadySet to apply customer side; Redwood will validate connectivity)
- Step 3: Exchange certs (if BYOK) and validate TLS handshake
- Step 4: Run smoke tests (Vivek’s list) and escalate any failing checks to Redwood oncall

Attachments attached in my earlier note: mutual-action-plan.docx — I can export a CSV of the egress IPs when we publish them.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sara Mitchell <sara@readysethealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:55:00 -0000
Subject: Re: ReadySet private deploy — final prerequisites and handoff

Quick clarifications from security/compliance side:
- KMS: If ReadySet chooses BYOK we require a staging key and an admin contact to perform an automated signing test prior to cutover. Rotation window recommended: 90 days.
- Audit logs: Please provide OC access for the first 30 days so our SREs can correlate request traces (read‑only). We will not retain customer logs beyond the agreed retention in the MAA.
- Data plane isolation: Confirm if you require tenant VLAN tagging or full L3 isolation — that affects routing and MTU expectations.

Also — egress IPs Ben mentioned are acceptable; once published we’ll provide the full allowlist and an example iptables snippet for on‑prem ops.

Minor ask: can ReadySet provide a short test account (non‑PII) with a sample workload so we can run the sample inference smoke test without hitting production data? If yes please send credentials to ops+readyset (ops email) using your secure channel.

Kimberly Park
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mitchell <sara@readysethealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: ReadySet private deploy — final prerequisites and handoff

Sara — thanks, appreciate the fast responses. Summary and next steps:
- ReadySet action items (due Wed 2026-11-18):
  1) Send production CIDR + confirm egress IPs you control
  2) Confirm KMS choice (BYOK or Redwood managed) and share test key or contact
  3) Provide non‑PII test account for smoke tests
  4) Share DNS delegation or cert owner for TLS automation
- Redwood deliverables (we will complete by Wed 2026-11-18):
  * Publish exact egress NAT IPs (Ben)
  * Provide iptables / firewall snippet and example IAM policies (Kim + Ben)
  * Run a dry run smoke test in a staging slice once test account is provided

I’ve penciled in a 30m cutover coordination call for Friday 2026‑11‑20 at 16:00 UTC — confirm if that works and I’ll send a calendar invite. If any of the checklist items will miss the Wed deadline, please flag now so we can adjust the cutover date.

Vivek
Director, Private Deploys | Redwood Inference
Attachments: mutual-action-plan.docx
